x: Gerry North was a good winner of this year's promotion from Adcocks (Coventry)and Edwards (Bristol) but despite Bill Kerr and Charlie Dabbs finishing 7th and 8th we were still pipped by Coventry in the team race.

However, we were still a minute behind the leaders due to a record breaking run by Adcocks of Coventry who reduced Ken Norris's 8 year old time by 16 seconds and took his club into a 22 sec. record lead over Derby with Portsmouth close behind.
Geoff split the Coventry team most convincingly,beating Kilby,Taylor and Heatley,but had to give best to Adcocks (an easy winner) and Horne who beat Geoff in the run in.

After one lap he was still in the twenties and although he began to make ground on the second circuit it was a slow and painful business against such opposition as Adcocks and Kilby (Coventry), Rose, Wheeler and Wyatt (New Zealand), Tulloh, Roberts and Barlow.

On the first leg of the return journey Adcocks ran for Coventry, Bruce Tulloh for Portsmouth and we had Hugh Barrow. Tulloh was in great form and took his team into the lead with a record breaking run which lowered the stage record by fifteen seconds.

Dick Taylor, their fast improving 5,000 metres runner will be a useful pacemaker for those marathon medallists Adcocks and Kilby. In addition,there is every chance that their cross country internationals Juan Taylor (only once outside the'teens in the last four Nationals) and John Hammond will be well to the fore.
For the early part of the race we were ahead of the winners Coventry, and their success seems to have hinged mainly on the good running of Dick Taylor (yet again) and Adcocks.
(Photo by Ed.Lacey)--Geoff North and Beevor(Herc/Wim) lead an impressive bunch early in the National Championships at Sutton Coldfield. Following up are Cox, Adcocks, Turner, Moxom, Ashton, D.
His invaluable effort left Derby trailing by 25 seconds, but Coventry's lead had been increased to 1:28 due to a scintillating run by Adcocks (27:09).
Since previous fast times on this course have been run by Kilby, Juan & Dick Taylor, Adcocks and Tim Johnston, this run of Gerry's is indicative of his present excellent form.

Yet there was contentment in the Belgrave camp on leaving Leicester; a feeling, perhaps, that we were the best team of the day and that Coventry, with those truly great runners Taylor and Adcocks, shouldn't really count against ordinary mortals.

…p of Dick Taylor - who on his own is worth 1½ minutes over the best of most other clubs - plus an extremely good run by Adcocks, who produced the second best time of the day, which brought about our downfall and we had to be content with second.…
